title: Base change of the middle exchange and projection composite
statement:
Fix distinct primes $p_0,\ell$, an integer $a\geq1$, $k_0=\mathbf F_{p_0^a}$, $k=\overline{k_0}$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, its valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $A_{E,m}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^m$ for $m\geq1$. Choose $\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$, $n\geq1$, and a six-functor datum [def-sf-datum] with the specified canonical transformations [def-exchange-projection, def-sf-pf]. All schemes and arrows below are separated and of finite type over $k$; all inputs lie in the displayed bounded constructible finite-Tor categories. Integral pullback and tensor are completed; field operations use rationalization and common finite coefficient fields. Let $f:X\to B$, $g:Y\to B$, $b:B'\to B$ be morphisms. Set $T=X\times_BY$, with projections $p:T\to X$, $q:T\to Y$. Put $X'=X\times_BB'$, $Y'=Y\times_BB'$, $T'=X'\times_{B'}Y'$; write $f',g',p',q'$ for the induced maps and $b_X,b_Y,b_T$ for the projections to $X,Y,T$. Let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$, $L\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$, $F=Rf_!K$, $K'=Lb_X^*K$, $L'=Lb_Y^*L$, $F'=Rf'_!K'$, $D=Lp^*K\otimes^LLq^*L$, and $D'=Lp'^*K'\otimes^LLq'^*L'$. Define just the middle exchange/projection morphisms
$$\beta_{f,g}=\operatorname{PF}_{q,Lp^*K,L}\circ(\operatorname{Ex}_{f,g}(K)\otimes1_L):Lg^*F\otimes^LL\longrightarrow Rq_!D,$$
$$\beta_{f',g'}=\operatorname{PF}_{q',Lp'^*K',L'}\circ(\operatorname{Ex}_{f',g'}(K')\otimes1_{L'}):Lg'^*F'\otimes^LL'\longrightarrow Rq'_!D'.$$
Let $\chi:Lb_T^*D\xrightarrow{\sim}D'$ be the canonical monoidal pullback comparison [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso], and let
$$\delta:Lb_Y^*(Lg^*F\otimes^LL)\cong Lg'^*Lb^*F\otimes^LL'\xrightarrow{Lg'^*(\operatorname{Ex}_{f,b}(K))\otimes1}Lg'^*F'\otimes^LL'.$$
The initial isomorphism is monoidality followed by the pullback-composition identification for $gb_Y=bg'$. Then the following equality holds as morphisms from $Lb_Y^*(Lg^*F\otimes^LL)$ to $Rq'_!D'$:
$$Rq'_!(\chi)\circ\operatorname{Ex}_{q,b_Y}(D)\circ Lb_Y^*(\beta_{f,g})=\beta_{f',g'}\circ\delta.$$
All exchange maps are the specified compact-support maps on the domains of [fix-lem-exchanges]; at finite pro-etale level the bounded etale-origin witnesses are retained, at the integral stage the strict reduction diagrams and completed operations are used, and at field stages the lattice and common finite-stage conventions are retained. The assertion concerns this middle square, before applying $Rg_!$, the outer projection formula or the compact-support compositor.

proof.text: Put $P=Lp^*K$, $P'=Lp'^*K'$, $v=Lb_Y^*$ and $w=Lb_T^*$. Write $c:wP\xrightarrow{\sim}P'$ for pullback composition, $r:vLg^*F\xrightarrow{\sim}Lg'^*Lb^*F$ for the comparison in the statement, and $\mu_{M,N}:v(M\otimes^LN)\xrightarrow{\sim}vM\otimes^LvN$. Let $e=\operatorname{Ex}_{f,g}(K)$, $u=\operatorname{Ex}_{f,b}(K)$ and $e'=\operatorname{Ex}_{f',g'}(K')$. Finally set $A=Rq'_!(c)\circ\operatorname{Ex}_{q,b_Y}(P):vRq_!P\to Rq'_!P'$. The pullback comparisons in the pasting laws of [fix-lem-exchanges] and the natural monoidal comparisons of [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso] identify $wD$ with $wP\otimes^LLq'^*L'$; composing $c\otimes1$ is exactly $\chi$. In particular $\delta=((Lg'^*u)\otimes1_{L'})\circ(r\otimes1_{L'})\circ\mu_{Lg^*F,L}$. All objects remain in the supplied domains of the datum [def-sf-datum].

source.place: Clause (iii), base change: PF for q and pasting of exchange over B′ → B; explicit middle-square calculation.

proof.text:
Apply horizontal exchange pasting [fix-lem-exchanges], clause 2, to the successive base changes $Y\xrightarrow{g}B$, $Y'\xrightarrow{b_Y}Y$ of $f$, and also to $B'\xrightarrow{b}B$, $Y'\xrightarrow{g'}B'$ of $f$. Both outer squares are the square for $gb_Y=bg'$; their upper-left corners are canonically $T'$. Clause 1 identifies their exchange maps through this isomorphism of square data, and clause 2 inserts the canonical pullback-composition comparisons $c,r$. Hence, as maps $vLg^*F\to Rq'_!P'$,
$$A\circ v(e)=e'\circ Lg'^*(u)\circ r.$$
The two uses of pasting have the same outer source and target; this uses horizontal base-change pasting, with no interchange of compact-support direct-image factors.

source.place: Clause (iii), base change: PF for q and pasting of exchange over B′ → B; explicit middle-square calculation.

proof.text:
Use the base-change square of [prop-sf-pf-coherence] with morphism $q:T\to Y$, base map $b_Y:Y'\to Y$, and inputs $P,L$. Its target comparison is $w(P\otimes^LLq^*L)\cong wP\otimes^LLq'^*L'$. Then apply naturality of the same proposition in the first input to $c:wP\to P'$. By the description of $\chi$ in step 1, the resulting equality is
$$Rq'_!(\chi)\circ\operatorname{Ex}_{q,b_Y}(D)\circ v(\operatorname{PF}_{q,P,L})
=\operatorname{PF}_{q',P',L'}\circ(A\otimes1_{L'})\circ\mu_{Rq_!P,L}.$$
Here the base-changed square is Cartesian since $T'=T\times_Y Y'$, and both $P$ and $L$ have the required finite-Tor domains by the supplied operation datum. No inverse projection formula or properness hypothesis is used.

source.place: Clause (iii), base change: PF for q and pasting of exchange over B′ → B; explicit middle-square calculation.

proof.text:
Precompose the equality of step 3 with $v(e\otimes1_L)$. Naturality of $\mu$ [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso] gives
$$\mu_{Rq_!P,L}\circ v(e\otimes1_L)=(v(e)\otimes1_{L'})\circ\mu_{Lg^*F,L}.$$
Functoriality of tensor and the equation of step 2 therefore turn its right side into
$$\operatorname{PF}_{q',P',L'}\circ(e'\otimes1_{L'})\circ((Lg'^*u)\otimes1_{L'})\circ(r\otimes1_{L'})\circ\mu_{Lg^*F,L}
=\beta_{f',g'}\circ\delta.$$
Its left side is the requested left side by functoriality of $v$ and the definition of $\beta_{f,g}$. This proves the equality at each coefficient stage directly: the cited exchange pasting and projection squares hold on the witnessed finite, completed integral, rational and common finite-field domains, and the cited monoidal comparison is the specified comparison at those stages. Thus there is no inference from equality after reduction to equality of integral morphisms.

This yields A∘v(e)=e'∘Lg'^*(u)∘r; I checked the directions of c and r.
